Our tool-use domain is synthetic (a mock CRM backend) rather than a real production system.

Up to 3 seeds and a 729-action space evaluated over 25–60 episodes per run in the main matrix is a reduced-but-transparent scope, not the full statistical power a longer study would give – and Section 5.2’s own result is that 25–60 episodes is provably not enough for the online controllers to reach their ceiling on this action space, which is itself evidence that a larger episode budget than we could run in this study would change (probably narrow) the gap we report.
Our unsupported-claim metric is a lexical-overlap heuristic for the retrieval domain only, not a general hallucination detector.

Our reading: this is not evidence that online context-policy learning is a bad idea: it is evidence that starting an online controller from a uniform prior over a 729-configuration space is sample-inefficient compared to a targeted, metric-guided search (BootstrapFewShot) that only ever proposes plausible demonstration sets.
lower token cost (e.g. tool-use on Bedrock Haiku: DSPy-static 96% success at 285 tokens/episode vs. REINFORCE 62% at 680).

A crash-isolation gap we found and fixed. Once we moved to the stronger Bedrock Sonnet model, jobs using plan and revise on the coding domain occasionally crashed entirely: a verbose reasoning field consumed the token budget before the required code field was emitted, and DSPy’s structured-output adapter raised on the malformed response.
post-fix, the affected jobs show a 2.5–7.5% adapter failure rate and complete normally.
A natural next step, which we flag as future work rather than claim here, is initializing the bandit/REINFORCE weights from the static baseline’s configuration instead of a uniform prior.
